title: Prerana Scholarship 2026: SC/ST ₹1,200, OBC ₹750 Monthly
meta_description: Prerana Scholarship Odisha 2026: SC/ST hostellers get ₹1,200/month, OBC ₹750/month, plus full tuition. Eligibility, portal, documents, rejection reasons.

hero.one_liner: Your family earns under ₹2.5 lakh a year and you've passed Class 10. Odisha's Prerana scholarship pays your full tuition and gives you a monthly allowance directly in your bank account. Here's what you'll actually get, what trips applications up, and how to apply without your form sitting stuck at the institute verification stage.

sections.heading: What Is Prerana Scholarship and Who Runs It
content: Prerana stands for Post-Matric Scholarship Registration Release and Network Automation. It is the Odisha government's post-matriculation scholarship program administered by the ST & SC Development and Minority & Other Backward Classes Welfare Department.

The scheme covers four student categories: Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), Other Backward Class/Socially and Economically Backward Class (OBC/SEBC), and Economically Backward Class (EBC). If you belong to any of these and you're studying after Class 10 in Odisha, this scheme is designed for you.

The scholarship does two things: it covers your tuition fees, admission fees, library fees, and sports fees directly with your institution, and it gives you a monthly maintenance allowance in your bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). The fee portion goes to the institution, the maintenance allowance comes to you.
All applications happen through the official Odisha State Scholarship Portal at scholarship.odisha.gov.in. There is no offline form.

sections.content:
Your institute must also verify your application online on the same portal, so you cannot do this entirely on your own.

One thing to understand from the start: Prerana does not send money to your parents' account or your guardian's account. It goes to the student's own Aadhaar-linked bank account only.

If you don't have a personal account, open one before starting the application.

The 2025-26 application window closed on March 6, 2026, after multiple extensions. New cycle dates for 2026-27 will be announced on the portal.

Check scholarship.odisha.gov.in for the latest dates because the department announces changes there first, not on social media or third-party sites.

sections.heading: prerana scholarship: All Four Schemes at a Glance
Who Qualifies: The Real Eligibility Picture
content: You must be a permanent resident of Odisha. Students from other states studying at Odisha colleges are not covered under Prerana - they need to check their home state's scholarship portal.
The income ceiling is ₹2.5 lakh per year from all sources for every category. This is the combined annual income of parents or guardians, not just the earning member's salary.
If your family has income from farming, rental property, or any other source, all of it counts.
For OBC/SEBC and EBC students: you must have scored at least 50% in your last exam. Falling below this blocks your application for that year.
SC and ST students have no minimum marks requirement, but you still need to be enrolled in a recognized institution.

Your course must fall under one of four groups defined by the department. Group I includes engineering, medicine, agriculture, veterinary, CPL, management PG diploma, M.Phil., Ph.D., LLM, and postdoctoral programs.

sections.content:
Group II covers pharmacy, nursing, paramedical, LLB, mass communication, hotel management, and most postgraduate degree programs like MA, M.Sc., M.Com., M.Ed.

Group III is the +3 degree program. Group IV includes +2, ITI courses, 3-year diploma, and 2-year vocational courses.

If you're in a short-term certificate course not listed in these groups, you're not eligible. When in doubt, check the official list at stsc.odisha.gov.in.

Your institution must be recognized and must be registered on the Odisha Scholarship Portal. Even if your course and category qualify, an unregistered college blocks your entire application.

Always verify your college's registration status on the portal before the admission process.

Students studying outside Odisha but who are residents of Odisha may be covered under the central post-matric scholarship scheme separately. Prerana specifically applies to students studying in Odisha.

sections.heading: The DBT Bank Account Trap: Verify Before You Apply
sections.content:
Your bank account must be in your own name, not your parent's or guardian's. DBT sends the maintenance allowance only to the student's Aadhaar-seeded account.

If your Aadhaar is not seeded with your bank account in the NPCI mapper, the payment fails after approval. You'll be approved on paper but receive nothing.

This is the most common reason students don't receive money despite having a valid application.

Before submitting: go to your bank branch, ask them to confirm your Aadhaar-bank account seeding is active. Don't assume it's done.

Confirm it in person.

sections.heading: Documents Required: Full Checklist
content: Gather these before starting the application: Aadhaar card of the student, income certificate from a government authority (tehsildar, BDO, or equivalent), caste certificate, and a copy of your bank passbook clearly showing your account number and IFSC code.

You also need your Class 10 (matriculation) certificate, the marksheet from your last examination, a passport-size photograph, and an Institute Declaration Certificate from your current college. Your college administration generates this certificate - ask for it well in advance because some colleges take two to three weeks.

If you have a disability, include a Divyang Certificate from the competent medical authority. Visually or physically challenged students also get a reader allowance of ₹1,200 to ₹2,400 per year on top of the regular maintenance allowance.

Every document must be scanned clearly in PDF format. The most common upload-related rejections come from blurry images where text is not readable, scans where the edges are cut off, and uploading in JPG format where the portal requires PDF.

sections.content:
The income certificate is the document most often questioned. An income certificate from a private employer or a self-written declaration is not accepted.

It must come from the state government - typically issued at the tehsil or block office level - and must reflect the current financial year.

Keep physical originals ready as well. Institutes sometimes conduct physical verification where they call students to cross-check uploaded documents against originals.

Being unable to produce originals can lead to cancellation at that stage.

One thing students miss: the income certificate must be in the parent's or guardian's name, not the student's name. A certificate that shows the student as the earning member gets flagged during district verification as it doesn't reflect household income.

sections.heading: Documents That Cause the Most Rejections
sections.content:
A caste certificate issued before 2020 is a top rejection trigger. Get a fresh one from the competent authority.

Your name must match exactly across Aadhaar, bank and mark sheet. Even a single-letter difference can block approval.

sections.heading: What 'Full Fees Covered' Actually Means in Practice
content: The phrase 'full tuition covered' in Prerana means the scholarship pays your college's tuition fee, admission fee, library fee, and sports fee directly to the institution. It does not mean a fixed rupee amount goes to you for fees.

How this works practically: the college submits your fee details on the portal, and the department disburses the fee amount directly to the college. You see this as a fee waiver or a credit in your college fee register, not as cash arriving in your bank account.
The maintenance allowance - ₹550 or ₹1,200 per month for SC/ST, ₹350 or ₹750 for OBC/EBC - is the portion that comes directly to your bank account through DBT. This is your actual cash component.
Exam fees are not always covered. Some courses have separate exam fees charged by universities that fall outside the scope of the fees listed in the Prerana framework.
Clarify with your college which specific fees are covered and which are not, so you're not surprised close to your exam cycle.

sections.content:
Hostel fees charged by private institutions can also fall outside the scheme's definition of 'admission fees.' If you stay in a private hostel attached to a recognized college, confirm with the district welfare office whether those charges qualify for reimbursement under your category.

The practical takeaway: treat the fee coverage as the bigger benefit and the maintenance allowance as the monthly cash support. Students who go in expecting large cash amounts are often disappointed.

Students who understand the fee waiver structure use it well to reduce what their families pay at admission time.

For SC and ST students pursuing Group I courses like engineering or medicine, the maintenance amounts are higher because the government recognizes that professional degree courses have higher living costs. But these amounts haven't been revised in several years.

If you find the amounts don't reflect current costs, the correct channel for feedback is the district welfare office or an official complaint through the portal.

sections.heading: Marks Cutoff and Category-Specific Rules: Quick Summary
sections.content:
SC and ST students: no minimum marks needed. Apply even if you passed with low marks.

OBC/SEBC and EBC students: you need at least 50% in your last exam. Below that, your application is rejected at the portal level before it reaches the institute.

All categories: income must be below ₹2.5 lakh per year from all sources. The income certificate must be from a government authority, not a private employer or a self-declaration.

sections.heading: Renewal: Do This Every Year or Lose the Scholarship
content: Prerana is not a one-time grant. You must renew it at the start of every academic year.
If you don't renew within the announced window, you lose the scholarship for that year with no exception.

Log in to scholarship.odisha.gov.in, select Renewal Application from the dashboard, update your academic details for the new year, and upload your latest marksheet and bonafide certificate from your current institution.
For SC and ST students, there is no stated minimum marks requirement for renewal. For OBC/SEBC and EBC students, falling below 50% in any exam can block renewal.
If your marks are borderline, talk to your college principal and ask for a written recommendation before submitting the renewal.
If you change colleges during your course, the scholarship does not automatically transfer. Update your new institution's details on the portal.

sections.content:
The new college must be registered on the portal and must re-verify your application before disbursement continues.

Taking a year drop or academic break cancels the scholarship for that period. If you return to studies after a gap, you need to reapply from scratch as a fresh applicant, not as a renewal case.

You don't retain your previous scholarship status across an interrupted enrollment.

Renewal works on the same portal, same login, same process as the original application. The main trap is missing the announcement window because the department sometimes announces renewal dates with only two to three weeks' notice.

Set a reminder to check the portal at the start of every academic year in July or August.

The maintenance allowance for renewal applicants is typically disbursed in quarterly or semester-based installments. If an installment is delayed, check the portal's disbursement status screen.

If it shows 'approved' but the money hasn't arrived, check with your bank that your Aadhaar seeding is still active - sometimes bank system updates reset the NPCI mapping.

sections.heading: How the Prerana Portal Works: What Happens After You Submit
content: Many students submit their applications and then wait without understanding what happens on the backend. After you submit, your application moves to three stages: student submission, institute verification, and district-level approval.
The institute verification stage is where most applications get stuck. Your college must log into the portal, review your application, and mark it as verified.
If your college has a backlog of applications or a single overworked scholarship coordinator, your application can sit for weeks without movement.
After institute verification, the district welfare office reviews the application. Officers check income certificates, caste certificates, and whether your course group is correctly filled.
This stage can take two to four weeks depending on the volume of applications in your district.

sections.content:
Once the district office approves, the department processes disbursement. Fee amounts are transferred to the institution.

Maintenance allowances are queued for DBT transfer to your Aadhaar-linked account. This final transfer can take another two to four weeks from district approval.

The total timeline from successful submission to money in your account is typically eight to fourteen weeks. Students who expect payment within a week of applying will be confused by the silence.

Track your status weekly on the portal and escalate only if your application status hasn't moved for more than three weeks at any single stage.

If your status shows 'rejected' without a clear reason, log a complaint through the portal's grievance module or visit your district ST/SC welfare office in person. The portal does not always send SMS or email notifications for status changes, so proactive checking is your best tool.

Save a screenshot of every status update along with the date. If you need to visit the welfare office, those timestamps help the officer quickly locate your application in their system and track where it stopped in the approval chain.

sections.text: Most rejected applications get blocked at institute verification, not at the student stage. Submit your application at least two weeks before the deadline and hand-deliver a printout to your college's scholarship coordinator the same day.

sections.heading: Why Applications Get Rejected and How to Fix Them
content: Aadhaar-bank account mismatch: the name on your Aadhaar must match your bank account name exactly, letter for letter. Even a difference in spelling or initials causes the DBT transfer to bounce after approval.
Fix this at your bank branch before applying.

Incomplete or unreadable documents: uploading a scan where the caste certificate number is cut off, or where the income figure is not visible, triggers rejection without explanation in most cases. Preview every uploaded file before submitting.

Wrong category selection: if your caste falls under SEBC but you selected OBC, or if you picked the SC scheme when you belong to ST, your application gets flagged during district-level verification. Match your scheme selection exactly to your caste certificate.
Duplicate applications: creating two accounts or submitting twice for the same year causes automatic disqualification. If you made an error in your application, do not create a new account.
Contact the portal helpdesk and ask for a correction.

sections.content:
Institute not verifying on time: this is the biggest cause of valid applications failing. The institute has a deadline to verify applications on the portal.

If they miss it, your application lapses. There is no way for you to force approval after the window closes.

Submit early and follow up with your college weekly.

Unregistered institution: if your college is not on the portal's approved list, your application cannot proceed at all. There is no workaround.

Verify before admission, not after.

Income certificate issues: using a certificate that is more than a year old, or one issued by a private employer instead of a government authority, causes rejection during document verification. Get a fresh income certificate each year you apply.

faqs.question: What is the prerana scholarship income limit?
faqs.answer: ₹2.5 lakh per year from all sources for all four categories: SC, ST, OBC/SEBC, and EBC. This is the combined annual income of parents or guardian from all sources including salary, farming, and rental income.

faqs.question: How much does prerana scholarship give per month?
faqs.answer:
SC and ST hostellers get ₹1,200 per month. SC and ST day scholars get ₹550 per month.

OBC/SEBC and EBC hostellers get ₹750 per month. OBC/SEBC and EBC day scholars get ₹350 per month.

All categories also get full tuition, admission, library, and sports fees covered separately.

faqs.question: Is 50% marks required for prerana scholarship?
faqs.answer: For OBC/SEBC and EBC students, yes: 50% in the previous exam is mandatory. For SC and ST students, there is no minimum marks threshold for initial application or renewal.

faqs.question: Where do I apply for prerana scholarship?
faqs.answer:
Apply at scholarship.odisha.gov.in, the official Odisha State Scholarship Portal. Create a student account using your Aadhaar, log in, and click Apply Scholarship.

There is no offline application route.

faqs.question: What documents are required for prerana scholarship?
faqs.answer: Aadhaar card, income certificate from a government authority, caste certificate, bank passbook copy with account number and IFSC, last marksheet, Class 10 certificate, passport photo, and Institute Declaration Certificate from your college. Divyang Certificate is additionally required for students with disabilities.

faqs.question: Why is my prerana scholarship amount not coming to my bank account?
faqs.answer:
The most likely cause is that your Aadhaar is not seeded with your bank account in the NPCI mapper. Visit your bank branch and confirm Aadhaar-bank linking is active.

Also check if your institution has completed its verification on the portal, as DBT disbursal only happens after both steps are clear.

faqs.question: Can students from private colleges apply for prerana scholarship?
faqs.answer:
Yes, if the private college is recognized and registered on the Odisha Scholarship Portal. Verify this before paying admission fees.

An unregistered college cannot verify your application, which blocks disbursement entirely.

faqs.question: How do I renew prerana scholarship every year?
faqs.answer: Log in to scholarship.odisha.gov.in, select Renewal Application, update your academic year details, and upload your latest marksheet and bonafide certificate. Renewal must be done within the window announced by the department each year.

faqs.question: What happens if my college does not verify my prerana application?
faqs.answer: Your application will not move forward and you will not receive the scholarship for that year. Submit early and follow up directly with your college scholarship coordinator, because the institute verification deadline cannot be extended for individual students.

faqs.question: What is the prerana scholarship portal website?
faqs.answer:
The official portal is scholarship.odisha.gov.in. This is the only portal for Prerana applications.

Do not use third-party websites claiming to help you apply - there is no such intermediary in the official process.
